 Order

The present petition under Section 482 of CrPC has been filed by petitioner Lavkesh Sharma against order dated 06-12-2022 passed by 8th Additional Sessions Judge, Gwalior in Criminal Revision No.
23 of 2021, whereby the revisional court allowed the revision filed by respondent by remanding the matter back to the trial Court for deciding afresh.

Facts giving rise to present petition in short that on 16-08-2007 complainant respondent filed a complaint against petitioner for commission of offences punishable under Sections 463, 464, 465,

sentences.text: Thereafter, a report was called for and on the basis of report, the trial Court found that the work of police personnel is very negligence and report has been prepared on the basis of forged affidavit of petitioner Lavkesh Sharma.
The trial Court took cognizance on the complaint filed by complainant and on the evidence of his witnesses.
The complaint filed by complainant on the ground that his father Babu Lal Batham has not executed any affidavit and petitioner got forged thumb impression of his father.
The learned trial Court recorded the statement of complainant and his witnesses..

After considering all aspects, the learned trial Court after collecting the evidence of respondent- complainant Gopal Chand Batham, and his witnesses did not find any offence prima facie against petitioner and complaint filed by respondent was dismissed vide order dated 08-01-2021 on the ground that merely on the basis of matching thumb impression of disputed affidavit with thumb impression obtained in Registrar's office by Babulal Batham (father of respondent herein) it cannot be treated that aforesaid affidavit was fraudulently prepared by petitioner Lavkesh Sharma and presented in police station and apart from this, it is also not noteworthy that in case of theft in which aforesaid affidavit has been stated to be submitted, Babulal Batham had sold said property to petitioner Lavkesh Sharma through a registered sale deed and seller Babulal Batham had made any objection regarding the above property during lifetime and no such fact has been brought on record.

As the aforesaid document being false or fabricated is concerned, prima facie no such reliable oral and documentary evidence has been produced by complainant to prove that aforesaid sale deed was prepared by petitioner Lavkesh by means of forgery.

Against the said order, the respondent filed a revision before Sessions Court and the Sessions Court allowed the revision filed by respondent by remanding the matter back to the trial Court with a direction to give an opportunity of hearing to the respondent and pass appropriate order afresh.
Hence, this petition.

It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that the respondent had filed a compliant against the petitioner regarding theft of grill but the Court dismissed the writ petition filed by respondent with a direction to proceed in accordance with law.

Thereafter, the respondent filed a private complaint which was dismissed by the trial Court and against the order of learned trial Court, the respondent filed a revision before the Sessions Court and the Sessions Court also confirmed the order of the trial Court.

It is contended that against the orders passed by the Courts below, respondent filed a petition which was also dismissed by this Court with a finding that the dispute is civil in nature, thereore, the same is not maintainable.

Against the order passed by this Court, respondent preferred a petition for recalling the order dated 18-05-2013 which was dismissed vide order dated 08-07-2014 and thereafter, the respondent filed a petition which was dismissed vide order dated 07-01-2015 and thereafter, also filed a civil suit before the civil court and the trial Court dismissed the application filed by petitioner under Order 7 Rule 11 of CPC and quashed the order of the trial Court on the ground that the suit is not maintainable.

Being aggrieved, the respondent filed a private complaint on the basis of disputed affidavit which was dismissed and being aggrieved, he filed a revision before Revisional Court and and revision filed by respondent has been allowed.

It is contended that the order passed by the trial Court is a clear abuse of process of law and without considering aspect, the Sessions Court has allowed the revision by remanding the matter back to the trial Court which is contrary to law.
The respondent is trying to make pressure on petitioner not to defence his right in civil suit.

It is further contended that in the affidavit of Babulal Lavkesh Sharma vs Gopal Chand Batham on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60839162/
2 no thumb impression was identified by anybody and it is clear from the affidavit that the said affidavit was identified by an advocate and same was executed before the notary.

sentences.text: It is further contended that without giving any opportunity or giving any notice, respondent got examined documents which is contrary to law.
Hence, prayed for setting aside impugned order passed by revisional Court.

Learned counsel for the respondent opposed the contentions of the petitioner and submitted that the revisional Court has rightly passed the impugned order by remanding the matter back to the trial Court in order to take cognizance against petitioner for alleged offences.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of this petition.
In support of his contention, he has relied on the the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of KT Joseph vs. State of Kerala and Another (2010) 2 SCC (Cri) 384.

entities.text: KT Joseph vs. State of Kerala and Another (2010) 2 SCC (Cri) 384
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of impugned orders passed by the Courts below as well as on going through the documents available on record, this Court is of the considered opinion that the trial Court after collecting the evidence of respondent and his witnesses has rightly found

that no offence prima facie is made out against the petitioner and the complaint filed by the respondent has rightly been rejected vide order dated 08-01-2021 and the revisional Court has committed an error in passing the impugned order while remanding the matter back to the trial Court for deciding the matter afresh

. Accordingly, the impugned order dated 08-01-2021 passed by trial Court appears to be just and proper and same is hereby confirmed and the order dated 06-12-2022 passed by the revisional Court is hereby set aside.
This petition deserves to be and is hereby allowed.
Petition stands allowed in view of aforesaid.
Let a copy of this order be sent to Courts below for information.
(DEEPAK KUMAR AGARWAL) JUDGE MKB Lavkesh Sharma vs Gopal Chand Batham on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60839162/
